set.body:
Source: plan phase 5.

Problem:
Vector[Byte] boxes. A 4 MiB log page costs roughly 5x the memory of the equivalent array, and FrameDecoder.feed is quadratic because it accumulates with buffered ++ input on every chunk. CommonLogRecognizer.recognize additionally allocates a second full boxed copy via map(asciiLower) before running eight naive searches with Vector random access.

Scope: 121 occurrences in main and 47 in test across nine modules (measured 2026-07-26).

Order: kernel -> core -> protocol -> interpreters. Each module compiles and its suite passes before moving on.

Hot paths where the benefit must actually be shown:
- FrameCodec / FrameDecoder.feed (replace the ++ accumulation)
- CommonLogRecognizer.recognize (drop the full boxed lowercase copy)
- CaptureState.append and SshCapture.append

Acceptance:
- Every golden fixture byte-identical before and after. That is the entire safety argument, and it is only available because P6f.30 landed on 2026-07-25.
- A recorded before/after benchmark of FrameDecoder.feed over a 4 MiB frame delivered in 64 KiB chunks, so the claimed win is measured rather than asserted.

Abort condition: if any fixture changes bytes and the cause is not immediately understood, stop and treat it as a wire change requiring its own decision.

Blocked by P7.3 (dependency decision).
set.title: P7.2: Replace Vector[Byte] with ByteVector
